subject: QPS partitioning anomaly — orchestration actions + customer note
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: QPS partitioning anomaly — observed asymmetric routing causing throughput drop for Checkoutly

Team —

We surfaced an unusual production pattern impacting Checkoutly (us-west region) starting ~07:50 PDT: overall QPS is steady but a large fraction is being routed to a small subset of serving shards, causing hotspotting and end-to-end throughput degradation. Checkoutly is on a high-priority committed capacity plan (DEAL-4392) and CS is already getting inbound alerts.

Immediate ask: can SRE + Eng triage root cause and implement a short mitigation by 9:30 PDT so we can avoid a restart or customer impact escalation? Product should sign off on the temporary routing change and the customer note below.

Observations (attached):
- qps-metrics-20280313.csv attached with per-shard QPS & tail latency time series
- Canary router snapshot (canary-router-snapshot.txt) shows active routing weights drifted to 3 shards instead of expected uniform distribution
- No obvious autoscaler activity (no scale events since 07:40)

Proposed mitigation options (pick one):
1) Short-term: force router redistribution to enforce even shard weighting for Checkoutly route (10–15 min config change, low-risk).
2) Fallback: shift Checkoutly traffic to smaller model variant (quantized) for up to 2 hours to relieve throughput pressure (needs Product sign-off for quality risk).
3) Rollback: if a recent rollout touched routing rules, roll that change back (requires change author).

CS / Sales: if we go with option 1 or 2, we should send a quick ops note to Checkoutly ops (draft below) — Marissa, can you review?

Ben / Karthik / Soojin: please confirm who will take ownership of the triage and estimated ETA. Include short runbook steps you will attempt.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: qps-metrics-20280313.csv (text/csv)
Attachment: canary-router-snapshot.txt (text/plain)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 08:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QPS partitioning anomaly — observed asymmetric routing causing throughput drop for Checkoutly

Received — I’m taking primary SRE ownership. Quick notes from initial triage: 

- Confirmed hot-shard behavior in us-west-2 between 07:48–08:20. The per-shard KV cache hit rates for the busy shards dropped ~15% while others were stable.
- Router logs show an increased retry loop for a subset of requests that correlate with Canary weight hedging. Suspect an internal routing policy mis-evaluation causing the router to prefer a small set of backends.
- No recent autoscaler events but pod-level memory for two serving pods jumped ~10% at 07:47; root cause TBD.

Immediate plan (attempting now):
A) Push a 'force-even-weight' override for Checkoutly route for 5 minutes and observe distribution (low-risk, reversible).
B) If weight override does not normalize tails within 10 min, temporarily enable per-route traffic limit (throttle) to shed tail requests and avoid queue blow-ups.
C) Collect heap/profile on the hot pods and escalate to Eng if we see KV-cache thrash or GC stalls.

ETA: A) within 7 minutes (pushed in 2 min), B/C dependent on results. I’ll post updates in this thread and PD incident.

Ben
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 08:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QPS partitioning anomaly — observed asymmetric routing causing throughput drop for Checkoutly

Thanks Ben — I’m on call for infra changes. Quick notes from Eng side after looking at canary snapshot + router evaluation logic: 

- Hypothesis: a recent change to the routing hedging heuristic decreased the penalty for connection latency, causing the decision tree to repeatedly prefer a particular backend subset when transient latency blips occurred. That combined with a tiny imbalance in active connections seeded the hot-shard behavior.

Planned remedial steps (I will perform with Ben online):
1) Apply router 'force-even-weight' override for Checkoutly (as Ben suggested) -> command: `rctl route set-weight --route checkoutly --mode force-even --duration 600s`
2) Recompute routing preferences and stream validation probes to all shards (we’ll run validation probes for 5 minutes).
3) If probes pass but tail latency still high, we will enable the fallback to quantized model variant for the Checkoutly route: `rctl route set-model --route checkoutly --model checkoutly-v1-q4f16 --duration 7200s` (Product sign-off required).
4) Capture heapdump and evacuation logs from the two hot pods and open ENG-PR ticket with logs for root-cause work.

Risk notes:
- The force-even-weight change is reversible and has low user-visible risk.
- The model fallback has quality risk (expected BLEU/quality delta ~3–5% for certain prompts). We should include that in the customer note if we take that path.

I’ll wait for Ben to confirm step 1 pushed; Ben, please confirm once done and paste the rctl command output here so Naomi/Marissa can sign off.

Thanks,
Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QPS partitioning anomaly — observed asymmetric routing causing throughput drop for Checkoutly

Thanks team — I approve the short-lived force-even-weight override (option 1). Please proceed and monitor quality metrics. If tails persist after the weight override and the fallback to quantized model is required, Product approves a limited 2-hour fallback window but only if:

- We include an explicit customer-facing note describing expected temporary quality delta,
- SRE/Eng track example prompts & quality metrics during the fallback, and
- We schedule immediate rollback if any automated QA checks exceed thresholds.

Customer ops note (draft) — please edit as needed before sending: 

Subject: Brief ops note — transient performance mitigation for Checkoutly
Hi Maria / Checkoutly ops,

We observed a routing imbalance in our us-west serving cluster that caused elevated tail latency for some requests this morning. We are applying a brief routing redistribution to spread traffic evenly across serving shards and expect normal throughput to return within ~10 minutes.

If tails remain, we may temporarily route Checkoutly to a quantized model variant for up to 2 hours to protect availability; this may slightly affect some generation quality. We will post updates in the incident and follow up with a technical write-up.

Apologies for the interruption — Naomi (CS) is on the thread for any immediate business questions.

Best,
Marissa (on behalf of Redwood Inference)

I’ve also attached a customer-brief-draft.md with slightly longer language if needed.

Marissa
Product Lead, Inference Platform

Update: force-even-weight override pushed at 08:37 PDT. rctl output below: 
`OK  - route checkoutly: mode=force-even duration=600s applied by ben@redwood.com at 2028-03-14T08:37:12Z`

Observability: within 90s we saw per-shard QPS distribute across expected shards and tail latencies started to converge. Heap/profile collection in progress on the two pods that saw memory jump. Initial heap profiles show elevated KV cache churn; sending logs to ENG ticket ENG-12456.

Next steps:
- Monitor for 15 min. If tails remain elevated after 15 min, Karthik, we will proceed with quantized fallback per your command.
- Naomi/Marissa: please hold off on customer note until we see how tails evolve in the next 15 minutes — I can signal to send the ops note if we enact fallback.

Ben
Senior SRE

Subject: Brief ops note — transient performance mitigation for Checkoutly

Hi Maria / Checkoutly ops team,

Quick update from Redwood: we detected an internal routing imbalance this morning in our us-west serving cluster that caused elevated tail latency for a subset of requests to your integration. Our SREs applied a brief routing redistribution at ~08:37 PDT which has already reduced tail latency and normalized traffic across serving shards. We will continue to monitor for the next hour.

If we observe persistent tails, we may temporarily fail over your route to a quantized model variant for up to 2 hours to protect availability; this would be a last-resort measure and could produce a small, temporary change in generation quality. We will only take that step with your approval and will send a follow-up note before making the change.

We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a short incident summary and any mitigation steps taken. If you’d like a sync, I can set up a 15-minute bridge.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
